Identify what each boundary and site is

Source: R/morphology.R
morphology.Rd

Before any rule can apply, every boundary has to be identified as a road frontage, side or rear boundary, and every site as a corner, through or rear site, with or without an access leg. These helpers do that, each returning the classification and the evidence for it, so a wrong call can be traced. All of them follow the same assumptions, from morphology_defaults(), a rulebook's morphology block and the morphology argument, in that order of increasing precedence.

Usage

find_road_frontages(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_side_rear(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_corner_sites(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_through_sites(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_rear_sites(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_access_legs(sites, roads, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_water_boundaries(sites, water, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

find_road_widths(
  sites,
  roads,
  centrelines = NULL,
  width_field = "width_m",
  rulebook = NULL,
  morphology = list()
)

site_metrics(sites, roads = NULL, rulebook = NULL, morphology = list())

Arguments

sites

An sf polygon layer of sites (or parcels) in a projected CRS, with a site_id column (created if missing).

roads

Road parcels (polygons), or NULL. Without them no boundary is a road frontage.

rulebook

Optional rulebook whose morphology settings apply.

morphology

Named list overriding individual settings for this run.

water

Water features (lines or polygons), optionally with a type column ("river", "stream", "coast", "lake").

centrelines

Optional road centrelines with a road reserve width column, see width_field.

width_field

Column of centrelines holding the road width (m).

Value

find_road_frontages(), find_side_rear() and find_water_boundaries() return an sf table of boundary segments; find_access_legs() an sf table of access legs; the others a data frame with one row per site.

Details

  • find_road_frontages(): boundary segments that run along a road parcel.

  • find_side_rear(): the other boundaries, as side or rear, from their angle to the frontage and how far back they sit.

  • find_corner_sites(), find_through_sites(), find_rear_sites(): site types, from the directions the frontages face and the frontage length.

  • find_access_legs(): the narrow strip by which a rear site reaches the road (a driveway or "battle-axe handle").

  • find_water_boundaries(): boundaries near a river, the coast or a lake.

  • find_road_widths(): width of the road in front of each site.

  • site_metrics(): area, frontage, depth, width and compactness.

Boundaries get one class, road, side or rear, and any number of tags (riparian, coastal, lakeside, reserve, zone_boundary). A setback rule naming a tag in its boundaries applies to boundaries with that tag, so a river boundary stays a side or rear boundary for every other rule.

Examples

town <- exampleton()
land <- town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ][1:60, ]
roads <- town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ]
head(find_rear_sites(land, roads))
#>   site_id frontage is_rear access_leg_area
#> 1 S000001 64.28599   FALSE               0
#> 2 S000002 20.52427   FALSE               0
#> 3 S000003 15.56643   FALSE               0
#> 4 S000004 16.77586   FALSE               0
#> 5 S000005  4.00000    TRUE              88
#> 6 S000006 19.21431   FALSE               0
legs <- find_access_legs(land, roads)
nrow(legs)
#> [1] 8
